model_meta.description: Inferred concept model of a vehicle-mounted stretcher suspension using linkages and spring means to permit movement of a stretcher-receiving member relative to a mounting base; pneumatic supply and height-control elements are optional claimed embodiments.

subsystems.description: Supports the suspension linkage on a vehicle floor and is shaped to engage at least partly about a floor wheel-arch protrusion; an open cut-away is a claimed variant.
Receives the stretcher and moves relative to the mounting base; claimed as a frame in an embodiment.

First and second link members use reverse fixed- and sliding-pivot couplings between base and receiving member. A third link is pivotally coupled between a primary link and receiving member; fourth and longitudinal transfer links are additional claimed variants.

Spring means mounted between linkage members to support suspension; pneumatic spring is a claimed form, including placement between first and second links or between the third link and a primary link in alternative claim arrangements.
Provides compressed air to the pneumatic spring circuit in the optional pneumatic-system embodiment.
Optional auxiliary tank connected to the pneumatic spring through a separate orifice plate component.

interfaces.interface_type: pneumatic connection from auxiliary tank to orifice plate

subsystems.description: Optional pneumatic circuit elements include height-control valve means, exhaust means, a raising/lowering control valve, rapid-rise and rapid-exhaust valves, and a lock mechanism isolating the spring circuit from height control.

External pneumatic boundary representing the destination of exhaust air; the patent identifies exhaust means coupled to the pneumatic spring circuit but does not specify the outlet destination or its physical form.
Orifice plate intervenes between the auxiliary tank and pneumatic spring in the claimed pneumatic-system arrangement; detailed flow behavior is not specified.

interfaces.interface_type: pneumatic connection from orifice plate to spring

item_flows.name: Base-to-linkage motion/load transfer
item_flows.notes: Fixed-pivot and sliding-pivot mechanical couplings; claims 1 and 14.

item_flows.name: Linkage-to-receiver motion/load transfer
item_flows.notes: Sliding pivots and other pivotal couplings permit relative movement; claims 1 and 14.

item_flows.name: Suspension spring force
item_flows.notes: Spring means acts between linkage members; claims 1–3 and 14–15.

item_flows.name: Compressed air
item_flows.notes: Optional pneumatic source, spring, tank/orifice and valve circuit; claims 8–13.

item_flows.name: Exhaust air
item_flows.notes: Exhaust means is coupled to the pneumatic spring circuit (claims 10 and 26); external destination is represented as a boundary and is not specified in the patent.

requirements.statement: The linkage shall permit the stretcher-receiving member to move relative to the mounting base.
The mounting base shall be arranged to engage at least partly about a wheel-arch protrusion in the vehicle floor.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1; open cut-away embodiment in claim 7.

steps.description: Fixed and sliding pivot couplings link the mounting base and stretcher-receiving member.
The linkage permits the receiving member to move relative to the base while spring means acts between linkage members.

At the functional level, the raising/lowering control valve controls movement of the stretcher-receiving member to and from ride height; the claims do not specify a valve sequence, feedback logic, or quantitative relationship.

At the functional level, the height-control valve means couples the compressed-air source to the pneumatic spring circuit, and exhaust means is coupled to that circuit; no operating sequence, feedback logic, or quantitative relationship is specified.
A lock mechanism can isolate the pneumatic spring circuit from the height-control valve means; rapid-rise and rapid-exhaust valve means are additional claimed elements.
